prompt: Generate a production material texture for the blank pages of a well-loved vintage travel diary, carefully kept for a few years. Quiet, refined watercolor-adjacent paper realism. Perfectly flat orthographic scan of a SINGLE portrait 2:3 sheet filling the whole rectangular canvas edge to edge. No background outside the paper, no perspective, no objects, no book mockup. Warm light parchment, muted oatmeal and light sand, approximately #e5d2b2. Lighter than antique brown parchment, yet clearly warmer than white or fresh ivory. Very fine matte rag-paper fibers and soft low-contrast natural grain. The center 92 percent is beautifully even and calm, an effortless background for small dark handwritten Vietnamese letters. A restrained touch of age only at the outermost 2 to 3 percent: slightly darker rubbed edges, softly rounded worn corners, one or two TINY short hairline creases, a few barely visible fiber specks. The page is intact and cared for. NO torn-off chunks, no ragged peeling layers, no frayed strips, no cracks, no holes, no dramatic rips, no foxing spots, no black dots, no large stains, no water rings, no dark vignette, no dirty mottling. Do not make it look like an ancient treasure map, ruined manuscript or distressed scroll. No yellow-orange cast, no gray cast, no white wash, no pure white center. No writing, text, numbers, lines, illustrations, motifs, stamps, border, glue, or tape. Flat even natural illumination, no cast shadows. This is a warm quietly aged book page, gently used rather than antique. LEFT book leaf: a very fine subtle binding crease at the extreme RIGHT margin, and minimal soft rubbing at the LEFT outside edge. A single delicate softened crease at bottom-left, just within the outermost corner. No conspicuous tear. Entire canvas stays opaque paper.
